simple.meaning: אַרְיֵה (ʼaryêh) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “lion.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 10 times across Daniel, beginning at Daniel 6:8. Its contexts include Torah, kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אַרְיֵה (H744).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: אַרְיֵה (ʼaryêh) / H744 is traced through Daniel 6:8, Daniel 6:13, Daniel 6:17, Daniel 6:20 as a generated source-based concept entry.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Now, O king, establish the decree, and sign the writing, that it not be changed, according to the law of the Medes and Persians, which doesn’t alter.”

timeline.evidenceText: Now, O king, establish the decree, and sign the writing, that it not be changed, according to the law of the Medes and Persians, which doesn’t alter.”

Then they answered and said before the king, “That Daniel, who is of the children of the captivity of Judah, doesn’t respect you, O king, nor the decree that you have signed, but makes his petition three times a day.”
A stone was brought, and laid on the mouth of the den; and the king sealed it with his own signet, and with the signet of his lords; that nothing might be changed concerning Daniel.

When he came near to the den to Daniel, he cried with a troubled voice. The king spoke and said to Daniel, “Daniel, servant of the living God, is your God, whom you serve continually, able to deliver you from the lions?”
Then Daniel said to the king, “O king, live forever!

Then the king was exceedingly glad, and commanded that they should take Daniel up out of the den. So Daniel was taken up out of the den, and no kind of harm was found on him, because he had trusted in his God.
Then king Darius wrote to all the peoples, nations, and languages, who dwell in all the earth:
Then king Darius wrote to all the peoples, nations, and languages, who dwell in all the earth:
So this Daniel prospered in the reign of Darius, and in the reign of Cyrus the Persian.
“The first was like a lion, and had eagle’s wings. I watched until its wings were plucked, and it was lifted up from the earth, and made to stand on two feet as a man. A man’s heart was given to it.
